sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 3.3% a year from $65.1 billion in FY2017 to $87.0 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F201].
FY2019 was the break: operating income fell 58.9% to $5.5 billion as an $8.3 billion impairment charge, including $6.8 billion of Shave Care goodwill, hit the year [F13][D97][X109][X112][P62].
FY2020 reversed it, with operating income up 186.2% to $15.7 billion, $8.3 billion of the increase from the base-period impairment charge [F14][D148][P71].
Since then the shape is steady rather than cyclical: operating margin has held between 22.1% and 24.3% in every year from FY2022 to FY2026 [F26][F27][F28][F29][F30].
The US was the growth engine over the window, rising from 40.8% of revenue in FY2018 to 47.9% in FY2026 [D512][D534].
In FY2026 the US added just 0.1pp of the 3.3% revenue growth while Non-US added 3.1pp on 6.1% growth [D536][D457][D511][D510].
FY2026 net sales rose 3% on favorable foreign exchange of 2% and pricing of 1%, with unit volume and mix unchanged [P26].
Beauty led the latest year, contributing 1.3pp on 7.1% growth, and Fabric & Home Care added 0.8pp on 2.4% growth [D603][D602][D543][D542].
Operating costs grew 2.1pp faster than revenue in FY2026, at 5.3% cost of revenue growth and 5.5% SG&A growth [D482][D472][D474].
FY2026 operating margin of 22.7% sat just above the 22.1% window median but 1.6pp below the FY2025 high of 24.3% [F30][D648][F29][D470].
The FY2026 decline came from a 1.0pp cost-of-revenue effect and a 0.6pp SG&A effect, as gross margin fell on unfavorable category mix and marketing spending rose [D483][D485][P25][P5].
Net margin of 18.4% sat 4.3pp below the 22.7% operating margin, with other non-operating income of $1.1 billion and a 20.8% tax rate partly closing the gap [F50][F30][D693][X108][D443].
That other income rose $922 million, driven by the prior-year Argentina translation charge and the Glad joint venture dissolution gain [P24].
FY2026 operating cash flow of $19.6 billion was 1.22x net income, against a 1.25x window median, and free cash flow of $15.1 billion was 0.94x [F80][F40][D444][D683][F100][D445].
Free cash flow margin of 17.4% was in line with the 17.2% median, and capex at 5.1% of revenue was 1.40x D&A [D441][D654][D440][D446].
Operating cash flow rose 10% as net earnings plus non-cash items generated about $19.5 billion, while inventories consumed $641 million and payables generated $919 million [P3].
Investing used $4.6 billion, primarily capital expenditures and hedge settlements, partly offset by Glad proceeds [P2].
The company carries net debt of $24.2 billion, or 27.8% of revenue on the pack's net-cash basis, against a 32.3% peer median and a 67th percentile among three peers [D450][D451][D695][D694].
Cash of $9.9 billion against $34.1 billion of debt leaves a 0.68x current ratio, below 1.0x and near the 0.63x window low [F140][D449][F180][D661].
FY2026 buybacks of $5.0 billion and dividends of $10.2 billion were 100.7% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count fell 1.3% [X134][X144][D453][D476].
Payout at roughly free cash flow with debt roughly flat means the buyback is funded at the margin by balance-sheet capacity rather than surplus cash [D453][D478].
The current ratio has been below 1.0x in every year of the window and stood at 0.68x in FY2026 [F180][F171][F172].
For a staples manufacturer with steady $19.6 billion operating cash flow, a sub-1.0x current ratio reflects working-capital structure rather than a liquidity strain [F80].
Buybacks plus dividends exceeded free cash flow in FY2025 at 116.6% and FY2026 at 100.7% [D402][D453].
Two years of payouts at or above free cash flow, with net debt of $24.2 billion, leaves little room if capex keeps rising [D450].
Whether operating margin in the FY2027 10-K holds above the 22.1% window median or slips toward the 8.1% FY2019 low would confirm or reverse the FY2026 cost pressure [D648][D646].
Whether capex stays above the FY2026 5.1% of revenue or falls back toward the 3.7% FY2021 level will show if the investment cycle is peaking [D440][D182].
Whether buybacks plus dividends fall back below the 100.7% FY2026 share of free cash flow would signal a shift toward debt reduction [D453].
